beginner.headline: Today (Tue Oct 13): conditional for beginners; your on-site check decides. South swell easing, still 14 s (NWS: south 3 ft at 14 s offshore). Canoes about 2–3 ft+ on the last third-party read (no timestamp). ENE trades 10–15 kt. Best 7–10 AM on the falling tide, before the trades fill in.
beginner.recommendation: Plan for 7–10 AM: the tide falls from the 5:42 AM high (2.1 ft) toward the 12:42 PM low (0.5 ft), so there is more water over the reef early, and the trades are lightest early. Watch several full set cycles first. The swell is easing, but 14–15 s sets still run above the average and push further inside. ENE trades of 10–15 kt are cross-offshore at Waikīkī, so expect seaward drift, more by late morning. The DOH list was not read, so check water color at Canoes and toward the Kūhiō drains and Ala Wai side; brown, gray or cloudy water ends it. One student or a small group of strong adults; several students or children only if sets stay small and drift is low. Your on-site read overrides this report.
